issues.legal_issue: Statutory acquisition interest is unavailable for a period before the preliminary acquisition notice when possession was taken before that notice.
material_facts: The claimant alleged that the land had been submerged before the acquisition process began and sought interest for that earlier period.
The land’s alleged submergence and the date possession was lost were disputed, and evidence indicated that the land may have remained in cultivation.
The High Court had awarded statutory interest from the date of the award.
issues.conclusion: Interest under the statutory interest provisions cannot be awarded for a period before the preliminary acquisition notice merely because possession was taken earlier.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, statutory interest runs from when compensation becomes payable, ordinarily from the award; it is not available for a period before acquisition proceedings begin. Lila Ghosh v. State of West Bengal and Special Land Acquisition Officer v. Karigowda support this rule. R.L. Jain v. DDA distinguishes pre-notification possession, for which rent or damages may be claimed, from statutory interest. The urgency procedure in section 17 is an exception under which compensation and interest may be payable from earlier possession; this case was not treated as falling within that exception.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: A claimant pursued an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.possession_preceded_notice: The claimant alleged that possession of the land was taken before the preliminary acquisition notice.
predicates.interest_claimed_for_pre_notice_period: The claimant sought statutory interest for a period before the preliminary acquisition notice.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns possession before the preliminary notice and interest is sought for the earlier period, statutory interest is unavailable before that notice.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner dispossessed before acquisition proceedings may seek rent or damages for the government’s pre-notification use and occupation of the land.
material_facts: The claimant asserted that the land had come under submergence before the acquisition notice and sought compensation for the intervening period.
The date and extent of submergence were not established; documents also indicated cultivation and other use of the land.
The Court directed the Collector to examine whether the land had been submerged and to determine the damages payable for the period before the acquisition notice.
issues.conclusion: The Collector must examine whether the land was submerged and, if so, determine the damages payable for the period before the acquisition notice.
issues.legal_principle: Where the government takes possession before a preliminary notice, title remains with the landowner, who may seek recovery of possession or rent or damages for use and occupation. The Collector may determine those amounts, with section 48 supporting that course. R.L. Jain v. DDA and Special Land Acquisition Officer v. Karigowda establish this distinction between pre-notification damages and statutory interest.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: A claimant pursued an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.pre_notice_government_use_alleged: The claimant alleged that the government had used or occupied the land before the acquisition notice.
predicates.submergence_or_possession_disputed: The parties disputed whether or when the land was submerged or possession was lost.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal involves alleged pre-notice government use and a dispute about submergence or possession, the Collector must determine the damages for that use.

issues.legal_issue: When pre-notification submergence is established, statutory interest may run from the preliminary acquisition notice rather than from the earlier date of submergence.
material_facts: The claimant sought interest from the acquisition notice through the award, relying on the alleged earlier submergence of the land.
The Court found no categorical determination that the land had been submerged before the notice and directed the Collector to investigate that fact.
The Court made entitlement to interest from the notice conditional on establishing that the land had come under submergence before the notice.
issues.conclusion: If pre-notification submergence is established, the claimant is entitled to statutory interest from the preliminary acquisition notice until the award, subject to the statutory requirements for interest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 governs interest on unpaid compensation. Lila Ghosh v. State of West Bengal, R.L. Jain v. DDA, and Special Land Acquisition Officer v. Karigowda establish that interest is not available under the Act for a period before acquisition proceedings begin, while the Court applied that rule to allow interest from the notice when the land had already been submerged. Section 23(1-A), as discussed in Siddhappa Vasappa Kuri v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, also uses the publication of the section 4 notice as the starting point for its additional compensation calculation.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: A claimant pursued an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.prior_submergence_established: The fact-finder established that the land had been submerged before the preliminary acquisition notice.
predicates.compensation_unpaid_after_notice: Compensation remained unpaid after the preliminary acquisition notice.

issues.definition: When prior submergence is established in a compensation appeal and compensation remains unpaid after notice, statutory interest runs from notice until the award.
